TeamActivity: the one-shot change-waiter registry behind wait_agent; timeout validated to 10s-1h, a single finish() closure closes the abort/timeout/notify race, close() wakes every waiter at disposal.

TeamError extends HarnessError with stable codes, plus errorMessage() rendering any thrown value as a bounded single line via node:util inspect (depth 4, compact) for durable records.

TeamService facade: owns roster/journal/task-board/activity, spawns teammates through ctx.subagents.startActivation, steers peer messages via steerHostSubagentPrompt, and registers the agentTeam projection; teams are implicit (Team id == root Session id).
TeamJournal: per-Lead transaction queue (transact) and appendAndFlush, which appends a team/* event and flushes the Session before notifying waiters, so a reader never sees an unflushed Team fact.

TeamRuntimeLifecycle: one AbortController as the admission cutoff, tracked operations, and withTimeout disposal; isCancellation walks the whole Error.cause chain so a wrapped cancellation is still recognised as expected.
readPersistedSession opens a short-lived persistence read handle, returns header + inheritedEventCount + events, and always closes the handle in a finally.

The agentTeam projection (stateVersion 4): folds team/* events, enforcing the member phase machine and contiguous task revisions, re-running the dependency validator on every task event, and memoising the wire view so mailbox-only changes publish nothing; a bad event stores a failure sentinel instead of throwing.

TeamRoster: membership resolution (a session with a subagent/descriptor is never a Team root), two-phase teammate provisioning (durable 'provisioning' before the child exists, checkpoint that the initial prompt was durably accepted, then terminal active/failed), and recovery from an orphaned provisioning member.
messageAccepted reconstructs the pending inbox from agent/inbox/spliced events so a message accepted but not yet run counts as accepted, which works against a persisted session read from disk.

TeamTaskBoard: the shared task DAG with eight actions, a compare-and-set expectedRevision fence, whole-value writes (revision+1), owner-or-Lead authorisation, and refusal to delete a task that still blocks a live one.

assertTaskGraphCandidate validates the complete post-mutation dependency graph (self-block, duplicate, missing/deleted blocker) and runs a two-phase DFS cycle check; called from both the command path and the projection fold.

Pure derivation of a task view: owner name, readiness (all blockers completed AND status pending), and ADVISORY write-scope overlap warnings computed on path COMPONENTS so src and src-old do not overlap.

Public Team vocabulary: branded TeamId/TeamTaskId/TeamMessageId, durable snapshots (TeamMemberSnapshot with a provisioning/active/failed phase) vs runtime views, service request types, and the four team/* session events plus the team-message message source.

requiredText and writeScope: write scopes are normalised to slash-separated workspace-relative prefixes and reject absolute paths, drive letters, . / .. and empty segments - advisory metadata, explicitly not a lock.

Durability suite: writes Team events, flushes, re-reads the persisted Session and re-projects, against the real SubagentService + spawn provider.
Pure fold suite driving teamProjectionDefinition.apply directly with synthetic events, covering every valid and invalid Team transition.

ActivationPool (Set of symbol slots, reserved before async creation and released after disposal), ChildLock (per-child promise chain that absorbs rejections in its tail), the Activation record with a WeakSet ancestry and a Session-id ownedChildren set, and the local failure observer that supersedes a failure on a later committed turn/end.

installSubagentArchiveAdmission answers workspace/session-activity with running descendants found by durable lineage (parentSession + origin subagent, any depth, never a fork) and cancels them on workspace/session-stop, one child at a time so a refusing sibling does not block the rest.

Canonical final-output selection: the LAST non-empty assistant message, else the accumulated assistant text stream; AssistantOutputFold folds session events or raw transport text (ACP chunks) into the same rule, independent of the stop reason.

Parent-owned durable subagent/catalog event and its chunked projection, versioned v0 (local modes) / v1 (unknown mode) / v2 (external), so discovery is one projection read that never loads a child Agent.

Shared in-process child composition: depth budget, durable session metadata, resolved child AgentOptions (latest logged request beats creation options; a route change clears the route-owned effort), the delegated policy capture (approval pinned to 'never' regardless of the parent's policy) written to the child's own log, and the SUBAGENT_DELEGATION_CONTEXT runtime contribution.
Type-only browser-safe barrel re-exporting the control types and the three projection view types.

Model-visible Team/Agent messages: the agent-message relay source (content the sender chose) and the distinct subagent-settled notice source (the manager stating what became of the child), plus the return guidance and the settlement notice that keeps only text blocks and states the terminal reason in the parent's own vocabulary.

Client-safe catalog rows, browser prompt/interrupt requests and receipts, and the closed Remote failure vocabulary (invalid-time-zone, parent-unavailable, not-resumable, unauthorized, attachment-invalid, delivery-unavailable); the prompt id shares the Session Controller's session-request-id brand.

validateControlRequest (Zod, stricter than the branded codecs) and rejectPrompt, which maps internal codes to the stable public ones and collapses DRAINING/ACTIVATION_CLOSING/ACTIVATION_LIMIT_REACHED/CONTINUATION_UNAVAILABLE/PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE into one delivery-unavailable.

delegationDepthOf takes the PERSISTED header as a monotone floor (runtime depth may deepen but never lower it) and validates the runtime value as a non-negative safe integer, explicitly rejecting -0; assertSubagentMaxDepth rejects any non-safe or negative cap.

The versioned (v3) durable subagent/descriptor event: a strict closed-schema validator over EXPLICIT fields rather than a merge-extensible options object, so an unrelated extension cannot break continuation; a different version folds to undefined and the first descriptor is authoritative.
SubagentError extends HarnessError with a stable code, so a subagent failure participates in the harness error taxonomy the tool layer reads to decide isError.

The Service Definition: ctx.subagents, a named-provider registry and a capability-validating start API. Method presence selects local (prepareContinuable) vs external (start) execution, a provider with neither is rejected at registration, the parent must be the EXACT live registry entry, the first unsupported capability is rejected, and the browser prompt path admits image parts through the attachment store before delivery.

Host-adapter seam: a Symbol.for marker on the standard send_message definition (so its model-visible schema is unchanged) and symbol-keyed Queue/Steer delivery adapters that avoid widening the public Service Definition.

Lifecycle-edge publication with per-listener exception containment, and epochStopReason which derives the terminal reason from the CHILD'S OWN LOG (never from teardown success), mapping blocked to refusal and any unnameable variant to error.

listChildren and listDescendants read parent-owned catalogs through a live-preferred observation that is released before the next branch; no Agent is loaded or resumed, external entries are leaves, an unreadable branch yields a diagnostic and root failures reject the whole listing.

The heart of the seam (1,493 lines): startup, admission, cold resume, capacity, ownership, settlement and disposal. Options and delegated policy are snapshotted BEFORE the first await; the capacity slot is reserved before async creation; closingScopes closes one exact parent tree's admission; watchLocalSettlement re-checks the Session sequence after the final flush; every unpublished failure rolls back and a teardown failure never replaces the captured result.

Shared out-of-process vocabulary: the frozen NO_START_CAPABILITIES, assertUsableCwd (absolute + enterable, probed with X_OK because a mode-600 directory would fail the spawn), settleRunResult (result NEVER rejects; failures flatten to stopReason 'error' and the diagnostic is bounded to 4096 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a sequence), and the idempotent subprocessRunHandle.

Client-safe projection vocabulary: SubagentCatalogEntry, SubagentTimingProjection and SubagentIdentityProjection (with the descriptor's seq so a consumer can prove the identity came from the child's OWN suffix); the subagent entry is null rather than undefined so it survives JSON.stringify.

The subagentTiming and subagent projections: every descriptor resets the timing state (a fork seed may carry an ancestor's), the identity fold is last-wins and never throws, and the no-value state is the serializable null arm so a pushed frame cannot carry a stale identity.

Child-scoped structured output: the tool validates against the schema, STAGES the value keyed by the ToolExecution object (adapter call ids can repeat), commits only on the authoritative tools/result notification, installs a terminal guard a later prepended listener cannot resurrect, and closes/reopens input on failure/commit.

Published contracts: SubagentProvider, SubagentStartRequest, SubagentResult, SubagentRun, SubagentActivation, the merge-extensible SubagentStopReasonMap, the four SubagentCapabilities, and ContinuableCreateSpec which is explicitly DATA and never a capability.

Proves the delegation policy is recorded on the CHILD's log before publication, asserting the event ORDER (sandbox/mode, approval/policy, permission/preset) and that fresh policy wins a stale fork seed.
Proves a child inherits its parent's preset composition by asserting the SCHEMAS in the child's own model request, loading the real preset registry through the production Loader.

The archive-admission contract with a hand-written Agent double: descendants reported at any depth but never forks, a looping lineage visited once, one throwing cancel not blocking its siblings, and the listeners dying with the service fiber.

Pins the final-output rule: the last non-empty message wins over later empty usage-only messages, reasoning deltas never enter the text fallback, and a reasoning-only message still counts as non-empty.
The catalog projection fold, chunk rollover, checkpoint restoration, and the external-membership arm; asserts the state changes only for new own facts.
Pins the child's AgentOptions inheritance (latest logged request beats creation options; a route change clears the inherited effort) and the depth validation for -1, -0, 0.5, NaN and Infinity.
The continuable-child policy suite: the seed, the approval pin, and the cold-resume case proving a resume replays the persisted snapshot instead of re-capturing the parent.
Proves a reasoning-bearing child's settlement notice can still be replayed through the DeepSeek adapter's default Messages path, using a real local SSE server.
Pins the exact settlement-notice content: text order and bytes preserved around omitted reasoning and tool calls, the input array not mutated, and the empty/reasoning-only arms.

Independent spawn presets and persisted-composition compatibility: an explicit same-as-parent selection is still independent, a fork whose selection follows its descriptor stays on the parent composition, and a missing preset projection refuses restoration.

The 4,044-line core suite: capacity, admission, cold resume, ownership, teardown, settlement delivery, lifecycle observation, errors and interrupt; uses a GatedAdapter, holdChildLock and managerState to place races that cannot otherwise be scheduled.

The browser prompt and interrupt Remote methods: payload validation, image admission through the attachment store, every stable failure code, non-canonical base64 refused without touching the store, and a non-owner caller recorded on the source.
Registered parent fixtures for the external suites: a hand-built Agent over a real Session with a stub inbox, so an external test drives no model.

External execution ownership: startup cancellation stays attached until cleanup, accepted work detaches from caller cancellation, disposal cancels the process exactly once, and a non-Error cleanup rejection is contained.

External admission across parent lifetimes: draining one parent's child does not cancel another parent's pending startup, and a repeated external id is rejected without disturbing its first execution.

A preset row standing in for agent-plane tool rows; plain JavaScript and import-free because the production Loader resolves entries through Node's ESM resolver, which cannot see the workspace's TypeScript sources.
The coding preset document: one agent-plane row mounting the preset_only tool, with the comment that the model-facing row lives in the preset, not in the host.
A second preset so a preset switch is a real switch - the tool a joined child sees has to change with it.

Discovery coverage including a migrated parent with V3 files and over 1,000 unrelated Sessions, proving listing neither enumerates the Session store nor loads a child; a corrupt catalog is reported and siblings continue.

Local backend fixtures: isolated JSONL persistence with onTestFinished cleanup, startTestActivation returning both id and localAgent aliases, and startPreparedActivation registering a temporary provider whose agentPreset capability reflects whether a seed was supplied.
Package-private access to the manager's resident map, locks and ownerCtx for deterministic race placement, plus dropActivation which removes only the map entry and leaves the Agent live.

Unit coverage of the shared out-of-process vocabulary: the frozen capability set, the cwd probe (with the POSIX no-search-permission case skipped on Windows and explained), the never-reject settlement, and the idempotent handle.
Parent result delivery independent of the child's messaging tool, parameterised over send_message being absent and merely unused - the promise holds in both.
Host completion racing around idle local children with preserved input: an idle-but-resident parked child keeps the host waiting, pinning the README's stated limitation.
loadStoredSession and seedStoredSession over a real persistence handle; both return inheritedEventCount, because the fork boundary matters as much as the events.
